correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier autocorrelation identity (six positive-difference representatives) and orthogonality reconstruct the fourth moment for all complex coefficients. Triangle inequality yields the nonnegative phase deficit. Writing A=1-s, x,y as axial squared norms and q,t as opposite-arm products, the magnitude fourth moment equals 1+2[A(s+2q+2t)+q^2+t^2+xy+4qt]. Since q<=x/2,t<=y/2, the max is bounded by 1+4s-11s²/4. Completion of square gives 27/11, with S=1. Every inequality difference is accounted for by an exact algebraic nonnegative identity; equality forces s=8/11,x=y=4/11,q=x/2,t=y/2 and affine phases, exactly the displayed orbit. Distinct frequency-difference residues for N,M>=5 give identical finite-grid proof. Standalone checker from actual artifact path passed 6,700 deterministic assertions, as corroboration only.
